items.summary: Extend the Motoko backend actor in backend/main.mo with user registration and admin-only functions: (1) `registerUser(name: Text, phone: Text, area: Text)` — stores a user profile keyed by the caller's principal, recording name, phone, service area, and signup timestamp; if the principal already exists, update the profile; (2) `getMyProfile()` — returns the caller's own profile as an optional record; (3) `getUsers()` — admin-only, returns all registered user profiles as an array; (4) `deleteUser(p: Principal)` — admin-only, removes the user profile for the given principal; (5) `deleteFeedback(id: Nat)` — admin-only, removes the feedback entry with the matching id (add an id field to stored feedback if not already present). Admin-only functions must check that the caller's principal matches a hardcoded admin principal constant defined at the top of the actor, initially set to `"2vxsx-fae"` with a comment instructing the deployer to replace it with their actual Internet Identity principal.

Add Internet Identity sign-in/sign-out UI to the Header component (`frontend/src/components/Header.tsx`). When the user is not authenticated, show a 'Sign In' button styled with brand colors (#FFD700/#FF8C42). When authenticated, show a small avatar icon with the user's name (if a profile exists) or a truncated principal, and a 'Sign Out' option inline or in a dropdown. Use the existing `useInternetIdentity` hook to manage auth state. On successful login, if the user has no stored profile (checked via `useMyProfile`), open the ProfileModal.

Create a ProfileModal React component at `frontend/src/components/ProfileModal.tsx` that appears as a centered modal overlay after first login when no profile exists. It must contain a form with three fields: Full Name (text input), Phone Number (text input), and Service Area (a select listing: Mahipalpur Extension, Mahipalpur Village, Aerocity, Vasant Kunj, Rangpuri, Nagal Dewat). A 'Save Profile' button calls the backend `registerUser` function via the actor, then closes the modal and invalidates the React Query cache for the profile query. A 'Skip for now' link dismisses the modal without saving. The modal must match the dark-themed design (#111111 background, #FFD700/#FF8C42 accents, white text, semi-transparent backdrop).

Create an AdminPage React component at `frontend/src/components/AdminPage.tsx` and add a `/admin` route in the application (using React Router or hash-based routing consistent with existing patterns). The page must: (1) check if the authenticated user's principal matches the hardcoded admin principal — if not authenticated or not admin, display an 'Access Denied' message with a link back to the homepage; (2) show a 'Registered Users' table with columns: Principal (truncated), Name, Phone, Service Area, Signup Date; (3) show a 'Customer Feedback' table with columns: Reviewer Name, Rating (stars), Message, Date, and a Delete button per row; (4) the Delete button in the Feedback table calls the backend `deleteFeedback(id)` function and refreshes the feedback list; (5) the Delete button in the Users table calls `deleteUser(principal)` and refreshes the users list; (6) both tables are fetched via React Query using the authenticated actor; (7) match the dark-themed design (#0d0d0d background, #FFD700/#FF8C42 accents, white text).

Add React Query hooks to `frontend/src/hooks/useQueries.ts` for the new backend functions: (1) `useMyProfile()` — fetches the authenticated user's profile using `getMyProfile()`, enabled only when the actor is available; (2) `useAllUsers()` — fetches all registered users using `getUsers()`, enabled only when the authenticated actor is available; (3) a mutation hook `useRegisterUser()` — calls `registerUser(name, phone, area)` on the actor and invalidates the profile query on success; (4) a mutation hook `useDeleteUser()` — calls `deleteUser(principal)` and invalidates the users list query on success; (5) a mutation hook `useDeleteFeedback()` — calls `deleteFeedback(id)` and invalidates the feedback list query on success. All hooks must follow the existing `useActor` hook pattern already present in the codebase.
